question: does global_optimization change anything on the pipeline's own data, and could a reader of the record tell either way?

probe_control.construction: two nodes, the second deliberately 0.5 off in x, with an edge asserting the relative transform is identity
probe_control.so: the optimizer moves a pose when the graph disagrees with its edges, and this probe sees it, so a zero correction measured below is the optimizer's answer rather than a probe that cannot read poses

demo_fragments.source: o3d.data.DemoICPPointClouds, the pipeline's own demo fragments
demo_fragments.why: the pairwise estimates are mutually consistent, so the odometry chain already is the optimum and there is nothing for the optimizer to distribute. This is correct behaviour and it is also why the capability was never exercised by a case where it could fail

through_the_product_pipeline.fragments: the three synthetic clouds the functional smoke writes
through_the_product_pipeline.so: the optimizer provably moved nothing, the smoke passed, and its success line still read that it had optimized a three-node pose graph

loop_with_overlap.construction: four 140-degree views of a cylindrical room at 80-degree spacing, so consecutive views overlap and the last closes back toward the first
loop_with_overlap.so: an edge the optimizer rejected leaves no trace in a record that serializes only the survivors, and the correction is still zero, so neither of the two things the optimization does is readable afterwards

through_the_product_on_a_loop.construction: the same four 140-degree views, written as PLY fragments
through_the_product_on_a_loop.why_this_case_exists: on consistent fragments the correction is 0.0 and nothing is prunable, so reading the poses after optimization rather than before, and publishing the surviving edge count as the submitted one, both produce identical output. This is the case where those two mutations are observable

what_the_record_omitted.a_keyword_scan_said_otherwise_and_was_wr: scanning the keys for 'before' matched fused_points_before_downsample, which is about voxel downsampling and not about edges. Recorded because it is the kind of false positive that makes an audit look complete
what_the_record_omitted.consequence: a run whose optimization corrected real drift and a run whose optimization did nothing serialize the same shape, and the smoke's success line says 'optimized a 3-node pose graph' either way

what_this_does_not_claim.not_that_optimization_is_broken: zero correction on consistent input is the right answer. The defect is that the record cannot distinguish it from a failure, and that no test exercised a case where the optimizer has work to do
what_this_does_not_claim.not_that_pruning_is_wrong: rejecting a loop closure that disagrees is the mechanism working. Dropping it silently is the part a reviewer cannot audit
what_this_does_not_claim.not_a_drift_correction_benchmark: these constructions establish that the measurements are missing and that the optimizer reads as a no-op on the shipped data. How much drift multiway recovers on real captures is a separate question
